claims.text: The target alloy is an Al-Cr-Fe-Mn-Ti quinary alloy with Al below 25 at.% and Mn above 15 at.%.
High-throughput screening identified Al-Cr-Fe-Mn-Ti candidates with melting temperatures above 1250 °C and specified L21 phase stability or fractions.
As-cast material may have a coarse microstructure and elemental segregation.
SPS at 1050 °C for 10 minutes with passive cooling will precipitate a tetragonal sigma phase in Al-Cr-Fe-Mn-Ti.
A controlled cooling rate after SPS can stabilize the sigma phase without dissolving it.
The proposed processing route will produce a refined BCC/B2 two-phase microstructure.
The SPS-processed alloy will contain a high density of grain boundaries.
SPS suppresses segregation in the alloy.
Sigma-phase precipitation and a finer phase distribution increase hardness relative to arc-melted material.
The sigma phase strengthens the alloy by acting as a barrier to dislocation motion.
A refined grain structure provides short-circuit grain-boundary paths for rapid Cr diffusion to the surface.
Rapid Cr transport forms a dense, continuous Cr2O3 scale that limits high-temperature oxidation kinetics.
The processed alloy will attain microhardness comparable to or above 475 VHN.
The processed alloy will show a 38–48% reduction in oxidation kinetics at 850–1050 °C relative to coarse-grained as-cast material.
Arc-melted counterparts have coarser phase distributions, lack the additional SPS-induced sigma phase, and consequently have lower hardness.
Coarse-grained as-cast material has poorer oxidation resistance because slow Cr diffusion permits non-protective spinel formation.
A processing window of 1000–1100 °C is suitable, with 1050 °C selected as the SPS temperature.
Cooling that is too rapid will prevent sigma-phase precipitation.
Extended exposure above 1100 °C exceeds the sigma-phase dissolution limit and may cause dissolution or transformation to another TCP phase.
The exact cooling rate needed to maximize sigma-phase formation without cracking is not established by the cited evidence.

contradictions.description: The target and baseline are specified as Co-free Al-Cr-Fe-Mn-Ti, but CoCr2O4 is given as an example oxide forming on the same-composition baseline; that cobalt-containing spinel cannot form without a Co source.

The intervention specifies passive cooling followed by a specific controlled cooling rate, while the conditions specify passive cooling to room temperature; no distinct controlled cooling stage or rate is defined.
